item.description:
Pancreatic cancer has been notoriously difficult to target and treat. wildpixel/iStock via Getty Images Plus For a long time, the likelihood of surviving pancreatic cancer has been extremely low. For patients who were diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer between 2015 and 2021, about 97% died within five years of their diagnosis. Pancreatic cancer is so deadly in part because there are no effective screening tests, and it rarely causes noticeable symptoms in its earliest stages. By the time a patient experiences signs, such as jaundice – a yellowing of the skin – or abdominal pain, the cancer has often already spread to other organs. item.title: Dolly Parton: The life of an iconic country singer
item.description:
Dolly Parton was just 5-foot-nothing tall. She needed platform heels to make her feel that she could fill a performance space. Her husband, Carl Dean, once told her that from the audience, her platinum wigs made her tiny figure look like a Q-tip. But no amount of mocking could make her surrender the hair, heels, and rhinestones, which were her own brand of feminism under wraps. “Believe it or not, I had to fight for that look!” she wrote in her 2023 memoir, Behind the Seams . The look wasn’t about showbiz. It was about sovereignty. And it must have been more than passingly rewarding for Parton to know that her audience finally understood this about her before she died, at the age of 80—to know that she was fully appreciated for the wallop of woman she was. She had so much guts, smarts, and self-ownership beneath the taffetized country-music artifice that sold more than 100 million…

item.title: Dolly Parton Knew What She Was Doing
item.description:
Ever since the news of Dolly Parton’s death on Tuesday, there’s one clip I can’t stop watching. It’s old footage featured in a 2020 documentary, and Dolly’s not singing in it; instead, she’s reading. “She pulled and she tugged. ‘I think I can! I think I can!’ she said”—and of course it’s The Little Engine That Could , the classic folktale made famous by Arnold “Watty Piper” Munk. Then Dolly turns to the kids huddled around her and says, “Would you help me? All of you, help me!” and she chants with them: “I think I can! I think I can!” Here is the thing about Dolly Parton: That woman understood the job she had been given to do, and she did it gladly. A lesser personality would have gotten buried under the piles of rhinestones and the 10-ton hair. Not Dolly.
